walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Volute CVC
walkthroughs.description: Learn how to track your cognitive process alongside your code

steps.title: Check Your Setup
steps.description:
Volute CVC needs a few components to work. Let's make sure everything is installed.

[Check Setup](command:volute.checkSetup)

media.markdown:
## Components

- **CVC CLI** (`cvc`) — Handles local repo setup, commit linking, and optional terminal history checks
- **CVC Language Server** (`cvc-lsp`) — Powers the extension
- **CVC MCP Server** (`cvc-mcp`) — Not needed for this VS Code workflow. Required only for non-VS-Code AI clients.

steps.title: Welcome to Volute CVC
steps.description:
Volute CVC keeps the reasoning behind your AI-assisted changes next to the code. In VS Code, the watcher reads GitHub Copilot chat session files stored locally by VS Code and links captured context to your commits.

[Learn More](https://cvc.dev)

media.markdown:
# Git, Augmented

Use GitHub Copilot in VS Code the way you normally do. Volute CVC reads GitHub Copilot chat session files stored locally by VS Code for this workflow, then shows the captured context in the timeline panel.

steps.title: Open a New Copilot Chat
steps.description:
Open GitHub Copilot Chat, start a new conversation, and work normally. The watcher reads Copilot chat session files stored locally by VS Code automatically - there is nothing extra to invoke.

[Open Chat](command:workbench.action.chat.open)

media.markdown:
## Watcher-Based Workflow

The VS Code watcher is built for GitHub Copilot's chat storage format and reads the local `chatSessions` files that VS Code maintains for Copilot Chat. It does not rely on a separate CVC chat participant.

steps.title: Open the Volute Panel
steps.description:
Open the Volute panel in the Activity Bar after a Copilot exchange. You should see captured thoughts appear in the timeline automatically.

[Open Timeline](command:volute.timeline.focus)

media.markdown:
## Pending Thoughts

Thoughts first appear as pending. After you commit, they move into commit-linked history for that unit of work.

steps.title: Commit, Push, and Review
steps.description: When you run `git commit`, pending thoughts attach to that commit. After you push and open a PR, the same history appears in hosted review as the shadow timeline.

media.markdown:
## From Local Thoughts to Hosted Review

The flow is simple: chat in Copilot, see thoughts in the panel, commit to attach them, then push and open a PR to review the same history beside the diff.
